# Blueprint 003: Copilot cache proxy

| summary | How PRD 004 is built: a same-binary sidecar (`pij-rs cache-proxy`) that holds one account's token and rewrites the cache TTL, and a daemon spawn gate that wires a Copilot Claude seat to it only when the sidecar says it is ready. |

<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

A new pi-free crate, `crates/cache-proxy`, carries the proxy: the request rewrite from the POC (`ttl: "1h"` on main-agent `cache_control` only, the client's own `X-Initiator` preserved before falling back to inference, `-1m` mapped to the base id), the token holder (`gh auth token --user`, in memory, refreshed only on a 401, single-flight), the readiness check (`copilot_internal/user`: endpoint plus quota; `/models`: limits), and an axum listener on 127.0.0.1:7471 that streams to the discovered endpoint with reqwest and follows no redirects. `pij-rs cache-proxy` runs it under its own LaunchAgent, so a daemon bounce never touches it. It serves a status route that the daemon reads: at spawn, to decide proxied or plain, and on one slow loopback poll, to give the prime one notice per state change. The daemon never holds the token.

| c-proxy-core | Proxy core (rewrite and pass-through) | module | crates/cache-proxy/src/{rewrite,serve}.rs | Ports the POC. Adds a missing `ttl: "1h"` only to ephemeral `cache_control` blocks of main-agent requests, and preserves explicit TTLs. Requests with `x-interaction-type: conversation-subagent` stay on the 5-minute default (req-14). A client `X-Initiator` of `agent` or `user` wins; if it is absent or any other value, the initiator is inferred from the last message (`agent` when it is all tool results). Maps a `*-1m` `model` to its base id (Copilot's API rejects `-1m` with 400 `model_not_supported`; the base id serves 1M). Otherwise streams requests and responses through unchanged (SSE, tool use, images, 1M context); a rewritten body is re-serialized deterministically, JSON-semantically equal, with object keys sorted (N001). Upstream redirects are not followed. Binds 127.0.0.1 only. | c-readiness | Readiness check | module | crates/cache-proxy/src/readiness.rs | GETs `api.github.com/copilot_internal/user` with the token: takes `endpoints.api` as the upstream, and `quota_snapshots.premium_interactions` as the quota (usable if `unlimited`, `remaining &gt; 0` or `overage_permitted`; otherwise the reset date). GETs `&lt;endpoints.api&gt;/models` for each Claude model's `max_prompt_tokens`. Checks are lazy and never block a status read: a successful check is cached 10 minutes per account, a failed one 60 seconds, and a refresh or a 402 schedules a recheck; a status read that finds a check owed starts one in the background, single-flight on the check lock, and answers from the cached state. Startup and reload run their check inline (F204, plan 230). An upstream 402 latches `quota_exhausted` with `quota.usable=false`; a lagging usable snapshot cannot clear it. Only a 2xx from a Messages POST, the quota reset date passing, or a reload clears that latch (F002). A 402 latches, and a 2xx clears, only when the request was sent with the token still held (same account and generation); an answer to a replaced token is logged with its account and changes no state (the 402 twin of F001, plan 230). | [req-04](../prds/004-copilot-cache-proxy.dd.md#requirements), [req-06](../prds/004-copilot-cache-proxy.dd.md#requirements), [req-13](../prds/004-copilot-cache-proxy.dd.md#requirements) | [ ] planned | — |
| c-status-route | Status route | endpoint | crates/cache-proxy/src/status.rs | `GET /__pij/status` on the proxy's port returns `{ready, state, reason, fix, account, upstream_host, quota: {usable, reset}, models: {"&lt;base id&gt;": {max_prompt_tokens}}, counters: {requests, refreshes, gh_launches, upstream_401, upstream_402}, pid, since, checked_at_ms}`. `models` lists only Claude ids, keyed by base id (never `-1m`). `state` is one of `ready`, `off`, `no_account`, `gh_missing`, `no_token`, `quota_exhausted`, `upstream_unreachable`. Types: `ready` is boolean and true only when `state=ready`. `reason` and `fix` are strings, empty when ready. `account`, `upstream_host` and `quota.reset` are strings or null; `quota.usable` is boolean. `pid`, counters and `max_prompt_tokens` are integers. `since` is epoch milliseconds of the last state change, not process uptime or the last check time. `checked_at_ms` (additive, plan 230) is epoch milliseconds of the last completed readiness check, null before the first. The route never waits on upstream: it answers at once from the cached readiness and, when a check is owed, starts one in the background (c-readiness); a status read during that check shows the previous answer. Failure mapping: missing config or account (or an unreadable config) -&gt; `no_account`; disabled -&gt; `off`; missing gh -&gt; `gh_missing`; token-fetch failure or a readiness 401 -&gt; `no_token`; no entitlement (a user response without `endpoints.api`, or a readiness 403/404) -&gt; `quota_exhausted`; network, timeout or 5xx failures -&gt; `upstream_unreachable`. `POST /__pij/reload` takes no parameters from a request body: it rereads the config file, refetches the token when the account changed, no token is held, or the last fetch or refresh failed, reruns readiness, and returns the status object. Neither route carries a token or a secret. | [req-04](../prds/004-copilot-cache-proxy.dd.md#requirements), [req-09](../prds/004-copilot-cache-proxy.dd.md#requirements) | [ ] planned | — |

A seat with no field (launched before the proxy existed) reads as plain. The route holds for its own launch's process, a same-process /new successor, or (F213, s08) a later process that descends from its anchor: spawn stamp or stamped-ancestor lineage. The anchor is the stamped launch process (pid and start time): for a gate stamp, the row's own verified process; a carried route records it (`cache_proxy.anchor`) and copies it unchanged on every later carry. Copilot's first CLI supervises its restarts (each restart is a fresh child of it and the previous restart's process exits), so restarts are siblings under the anchor, not a chain. The match is exact pid and start time against the kernel parent chain the daemon reads itself; the anchor is written only by the daemon, never from a claim, never self-reported. A route that turns plain (revive, gate fail, opt-out, a non-descendant process) is replaced, anchor and all, so a stale anchor never brings back proxied. A carried route reads `carried from its proxied launch through a Copilot restart; route not re-read` and counts as proxied for notices and the doctor. An opt-out holds in any new process. Self-report is impossible: Copilot runs extensions in a sandboxed host (COPILOT_EXTENSION_SANDBOXED) that gets no COPILOT_PROVIDER_*. | [req-04](../prds/004-copilot-cache-proxy.dd.md#requirements), [req-09](../prds/004-copilot-cache-proxy.dd.md#requirements) | [ ] planned | — |

A refused connection is declared `not_listening` at once; a timed-out or unreadable read is slow, and is declared `not_listening` only as the 2nd in a row (F204, plan 230). On each change of the declared state it sends one notice per change to each prime through `notify_prime` (crates/daemon/src/http/routes.rs), giving the number of live proxied seats and where to list them (`just doctor`), never their ids (notice noise, F192 class), and the fix; never repeats. Exposes the last status and counters, and slow reads apart (`slow: {count, last_at, in_a_row}`), in `/health`, so `pij-rs --json ping` and `just doctor` show them. | [req-08](../prds/004-copilot-cache-proxy.dd.md#requirements), [req-09](../prds/004-copilot-cache-proxy.dd.md#requirements) | [ ] planned | — |

<a id="decisions"></a>

## Decisions

| id | decision | why | realises |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| d-1 | A same-binary sidecar with its own LaunchAgent and port, not a task inside the daemon. | Prime ruling 5 (2026-11-18): a bounce closes the daemon's listener for only ~567 ms, but it cuts in-flight streams that run for minutes, and the daemon bounces several times a day. Same binary: no new artifact, and the Defender exclusion for ~/.local/share/pij/bin/pij-rs already covers it. | [req-08](../prds/004-copilot-cache-proxy.dd.md#requirements) |
| d-2 | The token lives only in the sidecar. The daemon reads the status route and never sees the token. | One holder means one place to audit (security verdict), and the daemon's logs and env, which reach every job it runs, can't leak it. | [req-02](../prds/004-copilot-cache-proxy.dd.md#requirements) |
| d-3 | Refresh only on a 401, single-flight, one retry. No proactive refresh. | Spike q-01: the `gho_` token is accepted directly, sends no expiration header, and the v2/token exchange returns 403. | [req-03](../prds/004-copilot-cache-proxy.dd.md#requirements) |
| d-4 | The quota check is `copilot_internal/user` `quota_snapshots`, not a model probe. | Spike: `/models` answers 200 with the quota exhausted, `/v1/messages` gives 402; `copilot_internal/user` shows `remaining 0, overage_permitted false` plus the reset date, for a free GET. Prime accepted 2026-11-18. | [req-04](../prds/004-copilot-cache-proxy.dd.md#requirements) |
| d-5 | A feature-specific config file (`~/.pij-rs/cache-proxy.toml`) set by `pij-rs cache-proxy account\|off\|on`, not a generic `pij config` store. | pij has no generic config store (its config is per feature, such as peers.toml); building one for two keys is scope the PRD doesn't ask for. Answers PRD q-03. | [req-02](../prds/004-copilot-cache-proxy.dd.md#requirements), [req-05](../prds/004-copilot-cache-proxy.dd.md#requirements) |
| d-6 | The gate's last word is the sidecar's own `ready`, read at spawn with a 1 s timeout; any failure means plain. | The sidecar is the only part that knows the token, the endpoint and the quota. A plain launch is always safe; a broken proxied seat never is. | [req-04](../prds/004-copilot-cache-proxy.dd.md#requirements) |
| d-7 | Proxy-death detection is a 30 s loopback poll from the daemon, not a push from the sidecar. | A dead sidecar can't push. One GET per 30 s, with no launch and no growth with seats, is the cheapest signal that also catches a hang. | [req-09](../prds/004-copilot-cache-proxy.dd.md#requirements) |

<a id="costs"></a>

## Costs

| id | what | rate | scaling | component |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| k-1 | Proxied model requests. | 0 launches per request; one upstream HTTPS request per seat request (the same request the seat would send directly) | with seat requests; adds no process | [c-proxy-core](#components) |
| k-2 | Token fetch and refresh. | 1 `gh` launch (absolute path) per sidecar start, plus at most 1 per 401 burst (single-flight); 0 per request | with sidecar restarts and 401 bursts, not with seats | [c-token-holder](#components) |
| k-3 | Readiness check. | 1 GET to `copilot_internal/user` and 1 to `/models` per 10 min per account while healthy and asked (60 s after a failed check), plus 1 of each after a refresh or 402; 0 launches | with accounts (1), not with seats | [c-readiness](#components) |
| k-4 | Spawn gate. | 1 loopback GET per Copilot spawn (2 after a timeout); 0 launches | with spawns | [c-spawn-gate](#components) |
| k-5 | Daemon's proxy watch. | 1 loopback GET every 30 s; 0 launches | constant: not per seat, not per pane | [c-proxy-watch](#components) |
| k-6 | Second-human-account check. | 1 `/usr/bin/dscl` launch per `cache-proxy status` or doctor run; never on a timer | with manual runs only | [c-proxy-verb](#components), [c-doctor-row](#components) |
